evals.prompt: How do I move an order to its next state without changing any of its data?
evals.expected_output: Runs cyoda-help.sh crud --section ENDPOINTS (one section, not the whole topic), answers that a named transition without a data change is PATCH /api/entity/JSON/{id}/{transition} with Content-Type application/merge-patch+json, If-Match: * (or the transactionId) and body {}, says that a PUT with an empty body is refused with 400 (as the section states), and ends with the source line naming topic, section, SOURCE and VERSION.

files._simulated/help.md: cyoda-help.sh prints SOURCE=instance VERSION=0.9.0 on stderr. `crud --section ENDPOINTS` returns the ENDPOINTS body, including the PATCH /api/entity/{format}/{entityId}/{transition} entry (merge-patch, If-Match required: a transactionId or `*`; the empty patch `{}` 'is how to fire a transition without changing the data; `PUT` refuses an empty body') and the PUT entry ('an empty body is refused with `400 BAD_REQUEST`').

assertions.text: Runs `cyoda-help.sh crud --section ENDPOINTS` (or another named crud section) before answering, rather than answering from memory
Reads one section (`--section`), not the whole crud topic
Answer is PATCH /api/entity/JSON/{id}/{transition} with `Content-Type: application/merge-patch+json`, `If-Match: *` (or a transactionId) and body `{}`
Says a PUT with an empty body is refused (400), as the crud help states
Ends with the source: topic and section plus SOURCE (instance) and version 0.9.0
Synthesises an answer; does not paste the raw help section

evals.prompt: What does WORKFLOW_SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED mean? I don't see it in the error list.
evals.expected_output: Runs cyoda-help.sh errors WORKFLOW_SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED (the code's own page). With no binary and no instance, the helper falls back to the web help mirror (SOURCE=web); the skill says so, answers from the mirror and asks the developer to type no command. Explains from that page that the code exists (400): the workflow `version` must be a supported MAJOR.MINOR, read from `cyoda help workflows schema-version versions`.

files._simulated/machine.md: `cyoda` is not on PATH. No profile has an endpoint. cyoda-help.sh prints SOURCE=web VERSION=0.9.0 and the whole web page for errors/WORKFLOW_SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED: HTTP 400, the workflow `version` is not in the supported MAJOR.MINOR range; see `cyoda help workflows schema-version versions`.

assertions.text: Runs `cyoda-help.sh errors WORKFLOW_SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED` (the per-code page) before answering
Answers from the code's own page (`errors WORKFLOW_SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED`): the code exists and means the workflow `version` is not a supported MAJOR.MINOR
Says the answer comes from the web help mirror because the binary isn't installed, naming the version
Points to `cyoda help workflows schema-version versions` for the supported version instead of stating a version from memory
Continues without asking the developer to type a command: no 'type `/cyoda:…`' or 'next, type …', neither in its own words nor in a warning it relays
Does not try to install cyoda itself

evals.prompt: Can I run Trino SQL reports over my entities?
evals.expected_output: Says 'SQL analytics is not available in cyoda-go 0.9.0' (the VERSION cyoda-help.sh reported; `cyoda help analytics` describes an interface cyoda-go doesn't serve) and gives the grouped statistics request (POST /api/entity/stats/{entityName}/{modelVersion}/query, from crud ENDPOINTS) or the search request (POST /api/search/direct/{entityName}/{modelVersion}, from search ENDPOINTS), with the request body taken from help.

assertions.text: Names or reads the help sections for the alternative it offers (`crud` ENDPOINTS grouped statistics and/or `search` ENDPOINTS)
Says SQL/Trino analytics is not available in cyoda-go 0.9.0 (the version cyoda-help.sh reported)

Gives the grouped statistics request (`POST /api/entity/stats/{entityName}/{modelVersion}/query`) or the search request (`POST /api/search/direct/{entityName}/{modelVersion}`) with a request body shaped as help describes it, as the way to report over entities
Does not give endpoints or steps from `cyoda help analytics`

evals.prompt: I'm writing a criteria handler in Kotlin. Exactly which fields does the criteria response need?
evals.expected_output: Gets the schema with cyoda-help.sh cloudevents json piped to jq for processing/EntityCriteriaCalculationResponse.json, reports required requestId and entityId, matches as required on every response except an explicit `success: false` one (the schema's if/then), and the optional reason (Cyoda keeps the first 2048 characters, per grpc COMPUTE MEMBER PROTOCOL), and mentions `cyoda-help.sh grpc proto` for stubs.

files._simulated/help.md: cyoda-help.sh cloudevents json prints {schemas:{...}}; schemas["processing/EntityCriteriaCalculationResponse.json"] has allOf [../common/BaseEvent.json], required [requestId, entityId], properties entityId, matches, reason, requestId, and if (not success == false) then required [matches]; the matches description says it is required on any response but an explicit `success: false` one. `cyoda help grpc proto` prints the .proto text.

assertions.text: Fetches `cyoda help cloudevents json` (via cyoda-help.sh) and selects `processing/EntityCriteriaCalculationResponse.json` with jq rather than listing fields from memory
Lists requestId and entityId as required, matches as required unless the response is an explicit `success: false`, and the optional reason
Points to `cyoda-help.sh grpc proto` (or `cyoda help grpc proto`) for generating stubs
Does not point to a GitHub schemas folder or a Cyoda-platform URL

evals.prompt: The workflows help says my compute node has to declare all of a processor's calculationNodesTags. Is that right?
evals.expected_output: Reads grpc --section "TAG ROUTING" (and/or workflows --section PROCESSORS, calculationNodesTags): a member matches when it declares at least one of the tags, the server picks round robin among matching members, and empty tags match any member of the tenant. Corrects the premise from the current help (both sections say at least one, not all) and cites the section it read.

assertions.text: Reads `cyoda-help.sh grpc --section "TAG ROUTING"` or `cyoda-help.sh workflows --section PROCESSORS` before answering
Says one shared tag is enough (overlap / intersection), not all tags
Says the current help (workflows PROCESSORS, grpc TAG ROUTING) states that one shared tag is enough, naming the section it read; does not call it a help erratum or cite #684
Mentions round-robin choice among several matching members, or that empty tags match any member of the tenant
